title: Single-Cell Optical Action Potential Measurement in Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiomyocytes
protocol: Reconstitute human iPSCs using small molecule modulation of WNT signaling and lactate purification techniques.
Maintain iPSC-CMs every 2-3 days with culture medium consisting of RPMI 1640 and 2% B27 supplement.
Prepare a storage medium for iPSC-CMs by mixing RPMI 1640, 2% B27 supplement, and ROCK inhibitor in a ratio of 1:2000.
Store the medium at 4 °C and use it at room temperature when needed.
Coat sterilized 10 mm round glass coverslips with 150 µL of factor-free basement membrane matrix diluted to a 1:60 ratio.
Incubate the coated coverslips at 4 °C for 4 hours.
Dissociate iPSC-CM monolayers using an EDTA-based cell dissociation reagent.
Ensure complete detachment by gently flushing with a pipette.
Transfer the cellular suspension into a 15 mL tube and add double volume of plating medium.
Centrifuge at 100 x g for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in desired volume of plating medium.
Count cells manually or electronically.
Select optimal density per coverslip (15,000 cells).
Calculate the volume of ‘active’ cellular suspension needed using a specific formula.
Calculate the volume of extra plating medium required and add it to the active suspension tube.
Apply the total cell suspension volume to each coverslip.
Regularly resuspend the tube contents to ensure even distribution of cells.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Gently fill the well with plating medium after incubation.
Exchange media with normal culture medium after 24 hours.
Maintain every 2-3 days thereafter.
Equip an inverted epifluorescence microscope with a 40x magnification, high numerical aperture lens (N.A: > 0.75).
Couple a fast switching warm white LED to the transmitted illumination port of the microscope.
Insert a simple red 660 nm filter into the transmitted light path for sample observation without contaminating the green fluorescent signal.
Mount a fast switching 470 nm LED head for photometry recording.
Insert a 470/40 excitation filter at the epifluorescent port of the microscope.
Insert a microscope cube containing a 495 nm long pass beam splitter in the mirror unit carousel within the microscope.
Fit a detection arm containing an adjustable field diaphragm to the microscope C-mount port to allow region of interest selection.
Couple a photomultiplier detector (PMT) and a USB camera to the microscope separately.
Insert a filter cube containing a 565 nm long pass beam splitter and a 535/50 emission filter into the PMT port.
Couple the PMT to a power supply and a PMT amplifier.
Connect the PMT amplifier output to an analogue input pin of a data acquisition system.
Filter analogue data from the PMT at 1 kHz or higher.
Digitize data at a frequency that is at least double that of the highest frequency present in the analogue signal (2 kHz or higher).
Prepare a Tyrode’s bath solution containing (in mM): 140 NaCl, 10 HEPES, 10 Glucose, 4 KCl, 1 MgCl2, 2 CaCl2, and adjust the pH to 7.35.
Warm the Tyrode’s bath solution to 37 °C.
Prepare an aliquot of loading solution by mixing 5 µL of 1,000x VF2.1Cl with 50 µL of 20% solubilizing poloxamer solution in a microcentrifuge tube.
Mix 5 µL of the loading solution with 5 mL of warmed Tyrode’s solution to achieve a final dye concentration of 0.1x in a 20 mm Petri dish.
Incubate a single iPSC-CM cover slip in the dish at 37 °C for 20 min.
Assemble a heated live cell imaging chamber and mount it onto the microscope stage.
Fill the chamber with 500 µL of fresh Tyrode’s solution.
Wash the coverslip with fresh Tyrode’s solution at 37 °C using fine point forceps.
Carefully apply the iPSC-CM coverslip to the pre-warmed bath chamber using fine point forceps.
Ensure the chamber and its contents are always heated at physiological temperatures.
Attach a stimulation insert with two platinum electrodes spaced 5 mm apart into the recording chamber.
Connect an external stimulator to the stimulation insert.
Set the stimulator to deliver 5 ms bipolar field pulses at 0.5 Hz.
Increase the stimulus voltage from 1 V upwards to determine the threshold stimulus, defined as the lowest voltage at which cells begin to contract.
Apply voltages roughly 25% above the threshold stimulus.
Fix the stimulation frequency with the external stimulator or trigger it with acquisition software.
Visualize myocytes in brightfield view using the transmitted light path and a USB camera.
Select an isolated cell and crop its optical path tightly with the field diaphragm to ensure only light from the cell of interest is monitored.
Activate the PMT amplifier and set the PMT supply to 750 V.
Run the stimulation protocol along with the acquisition software.
Simultaneously activate the 470 nm excitation light via a remote panel or automated at a fixed intensity (TTL signal).
Adjust gain and offset of the PMT amplifier to ensure the signal does not saturate.
Record 10 sweeps to detect stable action potentials.
Acquire background signal from a region devoid of cells.
Turn off the excitation light.
Locally perfuse reference drugs such as 1 µM nifedipine if desired.
Select a new cell and repeat steps for detecting cellular responses.
Swap out coverslips to ensure high experimental turnover in a single sitting.
Open a saved recording with analysis software.
Average 10 sweeps containing stimulated action potentials from a single cell.
Take the mean of the baseline signal representing Foffset.
Subtract the baseline signal (Foffset) from the averaged trace.
Calculate ∆F/F0 using the formula provided.
Identify the trace baseline (diastolic) and area of interest (AP).
Measure the decay time for 50% (APD50) and 90% (APD90) repolarization.
Export the data from this single cell to a spreadsheet software.
Repeat steps for all recordings.
Assess results with appropriate unpaired tests or analysis of variance.
